title: Formation of wide binaries by turbulent fragmentation
question: Did the wide protostellar binary IRAS 04191+1523 form by turbulent fragmentation, as tested by disk axis misalignment, young age and Keplerian-derived masses?

data.sensitivity: Cycle 2 rms: C18O 7, DCO+ 5, N2D+ 8 mJy/beam, continuum 1.0 mJy/beam; Cycle 3 continuum 0.45 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: The total mass of the protostellar envelope is 0.1 M$_\odot$(cite: Young2006).

what.value: Luminosities 0.6 and 0.04 Lsun for A and B

evidence.quote: The primary (protostar A) has a luminosity of 0.6 L$_\odot$, and the secondary (protostar B) has 0.04 L$_\odot$
The assumed dust opacity, commonly used for disks(cite: Andrews2005), is $\kappa_{1.3}$= 3.5 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ .

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux, size and inclination
recipe.method: Gaussian fits with CASA imfit on high-resolution continuum; inclination from cos^-1(min/maj)
Optically thin M = D^2 F / (kappa B(T))
assumptions: Tdust 30 K, gas-to-dust 100, kappa1.3 = 3.5 cm2/g, D=140 pc

recipe.method: Connect blue and red channel emission peaks per channel; mean and std for velocity shifts vs +-0.9 to +-1.4
Gaussian-fit peak positions of C18O along a line per velocity; fit Keplerian profile in peak position-velocity diagram; correct by 1/sin^2 i; only blue wing for B
assumptions: Edge-on for minimum mass; inclinations from continuum

evidence.quote: The difference in the projected position angles of the two disks is about 77$\mbox{$^\circ$}$.

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN parameters (cell, image size, masks, threshold, robust)
Continuum subtraction and line-free channels for C18O
Details of Keplerian fitting (fit function, how the peak positions were weighted, systemic velocity)
Why the Cycle 2 resolution is quoted as both 1.5'' and 1.2''
score_reason: Public data and simple analysis, but imaging and fitting details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple imfit and Keplerian analysis with numeric results, though some settings are unstated.
